Definition: middle voice from a compound of G575 and G3056; to give an account (legal plea) of oneself, i.e. exculpate (self):--answer (for self), make defence, excuse (self), speak for self.
BiblicalUsage: To give an account of oneself, to answer for oneself before accusers. Paul counts himself happy to answer for himself before Agrippa in Acts 26:2, and Jesus promises His disciples in Luke 12:11 that when they are brought before synagogues and magistrates they need not plan their answer. Paul says in Romans 2:15 that men's thoughts accuse or else excuse one another, and in 2 Corinthians 12:19 he wonders whether the church thinks he is excusing himself to them.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the word covers two courts: the one before men and the one inside me. Before men I may have to answer, and the Spirit will give the words; inside, my own thoughts accuse or excuse me daily. Paul's answer to both is the same — he speaks before God in Christ, for their edifying, not for his own defence.
